# Coordinator amendment: recovery and fixture repair

The user requested an actual repair rather than another unchanged retry. No analytics requirement, fixture threshold, accepted spec or task ownership was relaxed.

The worker command was pinned to attempt 2 after a newer attempt existed. Recovery now selects the highest numbered salvage ref, restores only assigned artifacts without staging or copying completed checkboxes, and saves assigned artifacts every minute while executing. An interrupted worker's attempt 4 was preserved before edits.

The unit guard emits a meaningful final failure summary. Launch refuses duplicate live runners and unresolved interrupted tasks. A separate Windows-launched supervisor records process exit; it never retries rejected work automatically. Short Windows temporary paths avoid the previous long worktree paths.

Deterministic recovery tests cover numeric ordering (10 vs 2), scope preservation, unchanged HEAD/index/checklist, and in-progress artifact copies. Fixture repair removes evaluator label hints from retrieval inputs, binds references to the worker grant, injects actual observable evidence faults, and tests numeric answers against rows and relevance against actual scope.

Only the six listed build scripts and their contract-lock hashes change. New scripts are now locked too. Build control recovery is distinct from product analytical reruns.

Additional verification: the launcher reads the authoritative sidecar state. Windows WMI launches a hidden supervisor independently of shell output handles; a real process smoke test confirms prompt return, logged output and recorded exit. All four recovery tests pass. Scoped periodic checkpoints are recoverable after a process crash and cannot replace a newer coordinator repair. The generic task command no longer contains an obsolete attempt reference.

Reviewed repair completion: this manually repaired unit may reuse actual Luna review evidence only when every assigned artifact, verification report, frozen contract revision and worker profile matches its attestation. Fresh unit checks still run, the runner still commits/merges, and any changed artifact or missing verdict fails closed. Other units retain normal Luna work and review commands. The final ownership objection is adjudicated against the canonical Primary owner table rather than supporting README case traces.
